The family originates from the need to accelerate the Marching Cubes algorithm, originally published by Lorensen and Cline in 1987 [Lookup Table and Ambiguity Handling](10327-lookup-table-and-ambiguity-handling.md).
The shift to GPU acceleration began with the advent of programmable shaders and compute shaders, allowing parallel processing of voxels.

Key developments include the use of append buffers for dynamic output sizes [GPU Marching Cubes (Compute Shader)](4687-gpu-marching-cubes-compute-shader.md), histogram pyramids for atomic-free counting [GPU Marching Cubes with Histogram Pyramid](2317-gpu-marching-cubes-with-histogram-pyramid.md), and capacity-safe pipelines for exact memory allocation [Capacity-Safe Marching Cubes Pipeline](4596-capacity-safe-marching-cubes-pipeline.md).
